title: SDK & Client Libraries: intake rubric and enterprise prioritization playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Create a repeatable intake and prioritization playbook for SDK and client library requests that balances developer experience, enterprise security/compliance needs, maintenance cost, and platform strategy. This will be the canonical process for PMs to triage incoming asks (language bindings, auth patterns, streaming ergonomics) and produce a prioritized roadmap with clear acceptance criteria and handoff to Eng/Design.

Problem: We receive inconsistent SDK requests from customers and internal teams: multiple language bindings, different auth workflows (SSO, token rotation, ephemeral credentials), streaming ergonomics (resume, backpressure, chunked events). Without a standard triage rubric, low-signal asks block engineering planning and enterprise needs slip through.

Goals:
- Define intake form + minimum metadata to capture business context, signal, and constraints.
- Produce a prioritization matrix with weighted criteria (customer impact, signal/usage, security/compliance, engineering cost, maintenance burden, strategic alignment).
- Enumerate enterprise-specific requirements (SSO/SAML, session rotation, audit logging, offline key rotation, VPC-friendly auth flows) and map to implementation patterns.
- Provide routing rules: when to schedule as SDK work, when to provide integration guidance (samples) vs full library.
- Deliver a playbook doc, recording template, and initial prioritized backlog for Q1 2026.

Acceptance criteria:
- Intake form in Confluence + Jamboard sample captured as link.
- Prioritization matrix agreed by Eng/Design/Sales with weightings documented.
- 6 initial triaged requests converted to backlog tickets with estimates and owners.
- Enterprise auth patterns library (mini-spec) created and linked to SDK implementation notes.

Proposed scoring (draft):
- Customer Impact (0-5) — direct revenue or blocker for a closed-won account (weight 30%)
- Request Signal (0-5) — number of customers or internal requests (weight 20%)
- Security/Compliance Risk (0-5) — required elevated controls (weight 20%)
- Engineering Cost (0-5) — implementation + maintenance (weight -15%)
- Strategic Alignment (0-5) — pushes platform capability (weight 15%)

Intake routing rules (draft):
- Score >= 3.7 => Scheduled as PM-backed SDK project (full library or major feature).
- 3.0 <= Score < 3.7 => Scoped as self-serve sample + prioritized SDK improvement.
- Score < 3.0 => Provide integration guidance and close with rationale, record as backlog low priority.

Enterprise auth patterns to standardize (deliverable: mini-spec for each):
- Long-lived API keys with last-rotate timestamp & audit log hooks.
- Short-lived tokens via customer-managed STS / token-exchange pattern.
- SSO/SAML onboarding flow and application-level role mapping.
- KMS/HSM-backed signing for on-prem/private deployments.
- Token revocation and graceful session expiry semantics for streaming connections.

Implementation notes (early):
- Streaming ergonomics: standardize a client-side SDK primitive for resumed streaming (idempotency + resume offset), and a backpressure / rate-limit signal wire spec; reference runtime streaming API.
- Language support: prioritize languages with production telemetry (Node, Python, Java, Go, .NET) but defer low-signal languages to community drivers unless enterprise sponsor commits.
- Auth SDK primitives should be modular: core request signer + pluggable credential provider for SSO/KMS.

Deliverables and timeline:
- 2025-11-20: Playbook draft (this ticket) + intake form link.
- 2025-12-05: Cross-functional review (Eng + Design + Sales + Security).
- 2025-12-15: Finalized prioritization matrix and initial backlog (6 tickets).
- 2026-01-15: First roadmap slot for highest-priority SDK item and enterprise auth mini-spec included in release notes.

Links & artifacts: 
- Intake form (draft): https://confluence.redwood.ai/sdk-intake-draft
- Prioritization matrix spreadsheet: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/sdk-prio-matrix
- Demo PR pattern for streaming resume: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-examples/pull/412
- Telemetry dashboard (usage by language): https://dash.redwood.ai/d/SDK/usage-by-language
comments: 2025-11-07 — Aisha Patel: Initial creation. Pulled 12 active customer asks from Support and AE. Note: several enterprise customers require SAML + token rotation for private deployments.

2025-11-09 — Liam Chen (Eng): Quick sanity check — we can surface a modular credential provider in the next SDK sprint but need design for streaming resume semantics. Estimate: 3 pt for core primitives, +5 pt per language binding for stable release.

2025-11-11 — Maya Singh (Security): Curious about audit logging expectations. For enterprise we need immutable audit events for credential rotations and streaming session start/stop; this will require runtime changes for private deployments. Marking security_review_required = true.

2025-11-13 — Elena Rodriguez (Design): Will draft a lightweight streaming UX pattern for client consumers. Need examples for: chunked events, reconnect, and client-side reconnect policy. Suggest canonical API surface: .stream() returns async iterator + .resume(token).

2025-11-15 — Ben Wallace (Sales): Customer ACME Corp is willing to sponsor Node + Java work if SSO and token rotation included. This moves the customer impact score to 5 for Node/Java. Adding as supporting evidence in the intake form.

2025-11-18 — Liam Chen (Eng): Follow-up — recommend we implement auth modularity first in Node + Python as they have largest telemetry. We can deliver a library pattern that other language SDKs can follow.

2025-11-19 — Aisha Patel (PM): Updated prioritization spreadsheet and routed this ticket for cross-functional review on 2025-12-05. Added initial backlog children tickets: PM-8892 (Node auth modularity), PM-8893 (Python streaming resume), PM-8894 (enterprise auth mini-spec).
